types.embedding_query_text: Company: A business organization that sells goods or services. Also called firm, corporation, enterprise. Examples: Apple, Nvidia, Micron, SK Hynix.

chosen_type.label: Corporation
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are major tech corporations; Corporation fits best.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

candidates.label: ComputerStore
candidates.comment: A local business specializing in the retail sale of computers and related equipment. Also called PC store, electronics store, computer shop. Examples: Best Buy, Apple Store, a local computer repair and sales shop, Micro Center. Distinct from Store, which is a general retail establishment.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

types.embedding_query_text: AIAssistant: A software agent that performs tasks or services for an individual based on commands or questions. Also called virtual assistant, chatbot, personal assistant. Examples: Siri AI, Siri.

chosen_type.label: SoftwareApplication
chosen_type.justification: Siri AI is a software application.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: ControlAction
candidates.comment: An action where an agent operates or manages a device or application. Also called controlling, operating, managing, manipulating. Examples: Turning on a light, adjusting a thermostat, launching a software application, steering a car. Distinct from Action, which is a general activity.

candidates.label: WebAPI
candidates.comment: An application programming interface that is accessible over web or internet technologies. Also called web service, API, REST API. Examples: the Google Maps API, the Twitter API, a weather data API.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: CheckInAction
candidates.comment: The act of an agent communicating their arrival and confirming a previously reserved service or place. Also called register arrival, confirm reservation, sign in. Examples: Checking into a hotel, checking in for a flight, checking in at a conference. Distinct from ArriveAction, which is simply arriving without prior reservation confirmation.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, someone. Examples: Michael Monaghan, Tim Cook, John Ternus, Benjamin Hall.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose, such as a business or institution. Also called institution, association, body. Examples: Founder ETFs, Segal Marco Advisors.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are organizations; Organization is the direct match.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

types.embedding_query_text: NewsOrganization: An organization that gathers and disseminates news. Also called media outlet, press, news agency. Examples: Al Jazeera, Reuters, Reuters news agency.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Al Jazeera and Reuters are news media organizations.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: ArchiveOrganization
candidates.comment: An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository. Examples: National Archives, a university special collections library, a corporate archive, a local historical society.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

types.embedding_query_text: StockIndex: A measurement of the value of a section of the stock market. Also called market index, benchmark, index. Examples: Nasdaq, S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, Dow Jones.

chosen_type.label: StockIndex
chosen_type.definition: A measure of the value of a section of the stock market.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for stock indices; minting with Thing as parent.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: PriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A PriceSpecification is a StructuredValue representing a price or price range, typically used for markup of offers. Also called pricing details, cost specification. Examples: a product's list price, a service's hourly rate, a discount price, a price range for a flight. Distinct from MonetaryAmount, which describes independent amounts of money.

candidates.label: PriceTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: PriceTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different types of prices, such as list price, invoice price, or sale price. Also called pricing category, cost type. Examples: list price, sale price, invoice price, suggested retail price.

candidates.label: ListItem
candidates.comment: A ListItem is an intangible representing a single entry within a list, such as a step in a checklist or a how-to description. Also called list entry, item in a sequence, element of a list. Examples: 'Buy milk,' 'Step 1: Preheat oven,' 'First item.' Distinct from ItemList, which is the collection of items.

candidates.label: TypeAndQuantityNode
candidates.comment: A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods within a bundle offer. Also called quantity specification, offer item details, bundle component. Examples: "3 kg of apples for sale", "2 units of product X as a bonus", "1 liter of milk in a grocery bundle".

types.embedding_query_text: Location: A place or position. Also called place, site, area. Examples: Cupertino, California, Cupertino.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific day in the calendar. Also called day, calendar date, specific date. Examples: July 30.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.embedding_query_text: Month: A period of about 30 days or one of the twelve divisions of the year. Also called calendar month, month period. Examples: October, September, May.

chosen_type.label: Month
chosen_type.definition: A period of about 30 days or one of the twelve divisions of the year.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for months; minting with Thing as parent.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: RelativeDate: A date expressed relative to a reference point, such as 'last month' or 'next week'. Also called deictic date, relative time, temporal reference. Examples: last month, last week.

chosen_type.label: RelativeDate
chosen_type.definition: A date expressed relative to a reference point, such as 'last month' or 'next week'.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for relative dates; minting with Thing as parent.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: One of the seven days of the week. Also called weekday, day. Examples: Friday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: Friday is a day of the week.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: PlaceOfWorship
candidates.comment: A PlaceOfWorship is a civic structure or building used for religious services and spiritual activities. Also called religious building, house of worship, sanctuary. Examples: a church, a synagogue, a mosque, a temple. Distinct from Museum, which is for exhibiting artifacts.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

types.embedding_query_text: FinancialReport: A formal record of the financial activities of a business, often released quarterly. Also called earnings report, financial statement, quarterly report. Examples: third-quarter earnings, Q3 earnings.

chosen_type.label: FinancialReport
chosen_type.definition: A formal record of the financial activities of a business, often released quarterly.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for financial reports; minting with CreativeWork as parent.

candidates.label: BankAccount
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct or service offered by a bank for depositing, withdrawing, or transferring money, often with interest. Also called bank account, checking account, savings account, deposit account. Examples: "My personal checking account", "A business savings account", "A joint current account".

candidates.label: FinancialProduct
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct is a Service provided by financial institutions to consumers and businesses. Also called financial instrument, banking product, investment product. Examples: A savings account, a mortgage loan, an insurance policy, a mutual fund.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: FinancialService
candidates.comment: A FinancialService is a LocalBusiness that provides financial services. Also called bank, credit union, investment firm, insurance company. Examples: A retail bank, a wealth management firm, an insurance agency, a loan provider.

candidates.label: MusicRecording
candidates.comment: A MusicRecording, as a CreativeWork, is a recorded performance of a musical composition, usually a single song. Also called music track, song recording, audio track. Examples: 'Yesterday' by The Beatles (the recorded version), a single from an album, a demo track. Distinct from MusicComposition, which is the abstract musical work.

types.embedding_query_text: Group: A set of entities considered together, often by a common characteristic. Also called set, collection, category. Examples: Magnificent Seven.

chosen_type.label: Collection
chosen_type.justification: Magnificent Seven is a collection of companies.

candidates.label: Collection
candidates.comment: A grouping of various items, which can include creative works or products. Also called assortment, compilation, set, aggregate. Examples: A collection of rare books, a stamp collection, a music album, a product catalog.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: SizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups used for various product categories. Also called size category, apparel size group, product size range. Examples: 'Adult', 'Kids', 'Petite', 'Plus Size'.

candidates.label: Series
candidates.comment: A general group of related items, which may or may not be of the same kind, forming a sequence or collection. Also called collection, sequence, set, installment. Examples: a book series, a lecture series, a product line, a collection of artworks. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is a series of creative works.
